publisher_scope: Publicly verifiable Oil India Limited, OIL subsidiary, regulator, government, court and supporting media event records. This is a reference corpus, not a complete internal OIL incident register.

coverage.counting_rule: One row per distinct incident or inseparable event episode; duplicate news articles, follow-up reports, aggregate safety tables and related sub-events are not counted as new incidents.
coverage.shortfall_reason: OIL does not publish a complete raw incident/near-miss census. Public disclosures are selective, and many older records are available only through regulator, government, court or media sources.
excluded_from_event_count: duplicate coverage of the same incident
non-OIL operators such as ONGC or AGCL

records.report_title: Fire at OIL Kathaloni-9 well
records.event_mechanism: Casing pressure rose and the drilling rig caught fire.
records.reported_narrative: A parliamentary answer records a fire at OIL well Kathaloni-9 on 21 June 1994. The fire reportedly took 27 days to extinguish.
response_and_investigation: Fire was extinguished after the reported 27-day response period.
immediate_underlying_causes: Casing pressure increase; detailed causal findings not stated in the source.

records.report_title: Rig-pump crane boom collapse at DET
records.event_mechanism: A rig-pump crane boom collapsed.
records.reported_narrative: A Gauhati High Court case records that Tilak Hazarika died on 15 September 2001 after the 12 September collapse, while Sangram Phukan was injured. The case also refers to OIL notices and an inquiry.
response_and_investigation: OIL issued legal notices and an inquiry was referenced in the court record.

records.report_title: Blast damaging OIL gas pipeline near Kathalguri

location.route: Duliajan to NEEPCO grid gas pipeline

records.event_mechanism: A blast partially damaged a gas pipeline; the report attributed the act to suspected insurgents.
records.reported_narrative: Public reporting described a blast on the OIL gas pipeline carrying gas from Duliajan toward the NEEPCO grid near Kathalguri.
immediate_underlying_causes: Suspected sabotage; not independently confirmed in the source.
source_discrepancies: Media reports describe the cause as suspected insurgent sabotage rather than a confirmed finding.

records.report_title: Simultaneous explosions damaging two OIL pipelines near Bordubi

source_discrepancies: The reported 16 injuries relate to a wider series and are not attributed solely to this OIL event.

records.report_title: Pipeline explosion near Lankashi tea garden

records.reported_narrative: A Lok Sabha answer records uncontrolled release from OIL Well 15 at Dikom on 13 September 2005, fire on 15 September, and extinguishment on 5 October.
response_and_investigation: The well fire was extinguished on 5 October 2005.

records.report_title: Crude oil pipeline leak and fire on Burhi Dihing river

records.reported_narrative: Public reports described crude leakage from an OIL pipeline into the Burhi Dihing river and a river fire that was brought under control.

records.report_title: Blowout at Baghjan Well No. 5
records.activity_context: Workover operations on a producing gas well.
event_mechanism: The well became active during workover operations.
Natural gas and condensate were released uncontrollably.
records.reported_narrative: OIL reports that Baghjan Well No. 5 became active during workover operations on 27 May 2020, released gas and condensate, caught fire on 9 June, was capped on 17 August and was finally killed with the fire doused on 15 November 2020.

reported_consequences.fatality_detail: Two OIL firefighters died while escaping the 9 June ignition; OIL's report also records another OIL officer death in the line of duty on 9 September.

response_and_investigation: OIL, ONGC Crisis Management Team, district administration, Indian Army and other agencies supported response.
A BOP stack was placed over the well on 17 August 2020.
Gas flow was diverted to the Baghjan EPS and flare pits on 13 September 2020.
The well was killed with brine solution on 15 November 2020.
OIL compliance reporting records bioremediation, plantation of 50,000 saplings and CCTV surveillance.
immediate_underlying_causes: Public authority material identifies deficiencies in planning, execution, procedure adherence and supervision; findings remain source-attributed rather than independently adjudicated here.
management_system_failures: OISD material identifies deficiency in understanding the gravity of removing the BOP without a confirmed and tested secondary safety barrier.
corrective_preventive_actions: Capping, killing, environmental remediation, plantation and compliance monitoring were reported.

related_sub_events_not_counted_as_new_in.description: Two firefighters died while escaping the fire; captured in primary event consequences.
Three foreign experts were injured during capping work; captured as a consequential sub-event.

preliminary_authority_findings.finding: Deficiency in understanding the gravity of removing the BOP without a confirmed and tested secondary safety barrier.
Deficiencies in planning, execution, adherence to procedure and supervision of the critical operation.

source_discrepancies: OIL News identifies two firefighter deaths on 9 June and one additional officer death on 9 September; OISD summarizes this as three employee deaths.

records.report_title: Uncontrolled fluid flow after theft of X-Mass tree at NHK-67
records.record_status: publicly documented in OIL press releases; reference-only
records.activity_context: Shut-in well security and well-control response.
records.event_mechanism: Miscreants reportedly cut and stole the X-Mass tree above the adapter, causing uncontrolled flow mainly of water.
records.reported_narrative: OIL reported that the X-Mass tree of shut-in well NHK-67 was cut/stolen around 9:30 pm on 19 October 2023. A crisis team and fire tenders responded; the well was capped after about 60 hours, killed and brought to zero pressure.
response_and_investigation: Crisis Management Team and fire tenders were mobilized.
The well was capped, killed and pressure was reduced to zero by 22 October.
immediate_underlying_causes: Reported theft/cutting of the X-Mass tree.
corrective_preventive_actions: Well capping and killing; security/investigation response reported.

records.reported_narrative: OIL's official press release reports a fire incident at its material subsidiary Numaligarh Refinery Limited; public reporting said the fire was brought under control.

records.report_title: Incident at OIL well plinth NHK 162
records.record_status: publicly documented in OIL Regulation 30 filing; reference-only
records.activity_context: Bleeding hydrotest water through a 2-inch bleed line.
records.event_mechanism: A 2-inch valve fitted to an artery-line connection and the bleed line unexpectedly dislodged while the valve was being opened.
records.reported_narrative: OIL reported that the dislodged valve and bleed line fatally injured a contractor employee nearby. The employee died at OIL Hospital at approximately 5:00 pm on 14 February 2024.
response_and_investigation: The employee was taken to OIL Hospital.
OIL announced an internal enquiry and recurrence-prevention measures.
immediate_underlying_causes: Valve and bleed line dislodgement during hydrotest-water bleeding.
corrective_preventive_actions: Internal enquiry and measures to prevent recurrence were announced.

records.report_title: Incident at BGN#24
records.record_status: publicly documented in OIL Regulation 30 filing; reference-only
records.activity_context: Wellsite production equipment at the X-Mass tree.
records.event_mechanism: A hole on the flow path from the X-Mass tree caused gas and crude oil leakage.
records.reported_narrative: OIL reported leakage at BGN#24, controlled by approximately 2:20 am on 10 April 2024. Gas and crude oil spread within approximately 100 metres of the wellsite.

reported_consequences.release_note: The press release does not state a fatality or injury count.

response_and_investigation: District administration and fire service were informed/mobilized.
OIL formed an on-site assessment team, began remediation and announced an internal enquiry.
The well was reported controlled and closed.
immediate_underlying_causes: Hole in X-Mass tree flow path; detailed failure analysis was not in the press release.
corrective_preventive_actions: Remediation and internal enquiry were announced.

usable_as: manual HSE review and schema development
not_usable_as: a complete OIL India incident or near-miss census
a statistically representative OIL safety dataset
data_quality.labels: No AI predictions, model scores, or expert SIF labels are included. SIF status remains unresolved.
data_quality.source_tier_note: First-party OIL records are preferred for event facts. Regulator, government and court records are retained as authoritative supporting evidence. Media-only records are retained as leads/reference records and are explicitly marked.
data_quality.coverage_note: OIL's public HSE materials describe incident/near-miss reporting systems, but the public site does not expose the complete internal raw corpus. Internal incident reports, near misses, unsafe acts and unsafe conditions are not included.
data_quality.aggregate_note: OIL sustainability/BRSR aggregate tables were reviewed for discovery but were not expanded into fake event rows.
data_quality.download_note: Seven source documents were already downloaded in the repository before this expansion. The additional source documents are preserved as link-verified provenance entries unless a local_path is explicitly present.
data_quality.document_note: The JSON stores normalized facts and provenance. It does not reproduce copyrighted source articles or full PDF text. All source links are retained in source_documents.
